name: Buu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Buu (Cameroon) undescribed; Voll 2017 (Mundabli grammar) only argues Buu is a distinct language (pp.6-7), no Buu phonology

new_statements.quote: Comme la plupart des langues africaines, le bu est une langue à tons. En effet, le ton joue un rôle très distinctif dans cette langue, dans le sens où un changement de ton peut entraîner un changement de sens : il a donc une valeur lexicale. [...] Dans la forme sous-jacente, le bu est une langue à deux tons, à savoir les tons haut (H) et bas (B) bien que nous retrouvons les autres tons tels que le ton moyen (M) et les tons modulés au niveau phonétique.
new_statements.translation: Like most African languages, Bu is a tone language. Indeed, tone plays a highly distinctive role in this language, in the sense that a change of tone can bring about a change of meaning: it therefore has lexical value. [...] Underlyingly, Bu is a two-tone language, namely the tones high (H) and low (B), although we find the other tones such as mid (M) and the contour tones at the phonetic level.
new_statements.citation: Ngako Yonga, Monique Doriane. 2013. Ebauche phonologique et morphologique de la langue bu. Mémoire de Master, Université de Yaoundé I. §2.3 'Les tons du bu', pp. 17-18 (PDF pp. 30-31).
new_statements.locator: §2.3 Les tons du bu, pp. 17-18 (PDF pp. 30-31); tone tables §2.3.1-2.3.2 pp. 18-20
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (153 pp., iText 2013; body text layer is a glyph-cipher font, so I rendered the pages with page render and read the images). Thesis p. 17 (PDF p. 30), heading "2.3. Les tons du bu": "Comme la plupart des langues africaines, le bu est une langue à tons. En effet, le ton joue un rôle très distinctif dans cette langue, dans le sens où un changement de ton peut entraîner un changement de sens : il a donc une valeur lexicale." -- verbatim. Thesis p. 18 (PDF p. 31), after minimal pairs (10) jèn/jén, tà/tá, dʒí/dʒì: "Dans la forme sous-jacente, le bu est une langue à deux tons, à savoir les tons haut (H) et bas (B) bien que nous retrouvons les autres tons tels que le ton moyen (M) et les to…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Buu is described as a lexical tone language with two underlying tones (H, L), mid tone and rising/falling contours being phonetic derivatives (default tones, floating tones from glided or elided vowels). The only phonological description of the language contains no statement of any kind about word stress or accent; no stress rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress statement to have exceptions). The one occurrence of 'stress' (p. 66) refers to English as a stress language when discussing loanwords.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statements concern lexical items (noun and verb roots, citation forms elicited from a c.1500-word questionnaire and interviews); also grammatical tone in verb conjugation (ch. 5). Nothing at word level about stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Buu of Lower Fungom (village of Buu, Fungom Subdivision, Menchum Division, NW Cameroon), the divergent member of the 'Ji group' (Mundabli-Mufu and Buu); Ethnologue subsumes it under Mundabli [boe], but Good et al. 2011, Ngako Yonga 2013 and Voll 2017 treat it as a separate language. The thesis spells the name 'bu' (author argues the language has no long vowels). Not Bu [jid] of Nigeria (buuu1244) nor the Laimbue-speaking village Bu south of Wum.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid page buuu1246 (Buu), with subclassification comment citing Voll 2017: 6-7, Good et al. 2011: 124-125, Hamm et al. 2002.
sources.note: No descriptive references listed for the languoid; Ngako Yonga 2013 is absent from Glottolog.

sources.citation: Voll, Rebecca. 2017. A grammar of Mundabli, a Bantoid (Yemne-Kimbi) language of Cameroon. PhD dissertation, Leiden University (LOT 471).
sources.note: Describes Mundabli, not Buu. pp. 5-7 argue Buu is a separate language; p. 7 and p. 80 n.2 identify Ngako Yonga 2013 as the phonological and morphological sketch of Buu; p. 42 n.14 Buu imperfective -kə from Voll's own fieldwork + Ngako. No stress statement about Buu (or Mundabli; 'stress' only in non-technical uses).

sources.citation: Ngako Yonga, Monique Doriane. 2013 [acad. year 2011-2012]. Ebauche phonologique et morphologique de la langue bu. Mémoire de Master (linguistique générale, option phonologie), dir. N. P. Mutaka. Université de Yaoundé I. XII + c.140 pp. (153 PDF pp.)
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. §2.3 'Les tons du bu' (pp. 17-20): Buu is a tone language with two underlying tones H and B (low); phonetic M and rising/falling contours derived. Ch. 4-5 lexical tone on nouns and verbs. The only occurrence of 'stress' (p. 66, PDF 79) is about English being a stress rather than tone language when discussing loanwords. Body text layer uses unmapped glyph codes; decoded by substitution and checked against page images (pp. 17-18).

sources.citation: Di Carlo, Pierpaolo & Jeff Good. 2012. What are we trying to preserve? Diversity, change, and ideology at the edge of the Cameroonian Grassfields. Ms., University at Buffalo (Glottolog ref 675213).
sources.note: Language ideology / sociolinguistics; Buu named as probably a separate language from Mundabli-Mufu; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Good, Jeff, Jesse Lovegren, Jean Patrick Mve, Carine Nguanguep Tchiemouo, Rebecca Voll & Pierpaolo Di Carlo. 2011. The languages of the Lower Fungom region of Cameroon: Grammatical overview. Africana Linguistica 17: 101-164.
sources.note: §3.3 'Mundabli-Mufu and Buu: the Ji group' (pp. 124-129): the phonology given (consonants, vowels, 4 tone levels) is explicitly Mundabli only ('coverage of the other varieties will have to await future work', p. 125); earlier Buu sources named are Hombert 1980 (noun classes) and Hamm et al. 2002: 30-32 (wordlist). No stress statement for any language.
